section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate
section_1.content: Briefly visualize the derivative as the 'speedometer' of a function. Introduce the concept of a function machine: an input x goes in, f(x) comes out. Emphasize that we are now looking at functions within functions (nested) and products of functions.
section_1.example: An animation of a car's speed (derivative) changing as it travels along a winding road.

section_2.title: The Product Rule: The Collaborative Duo
section_2.content: When two functions, u(x) and v(x), are multiplied, the derivative isn't just the product of their derivatives. Use an area-model animation: a rectangle with sides u(x) and v(x) expanding. The change in area is the sum of two strips: u(x)dv + v(x)du.
section_2.example: A cat running (function u) while carrying a toy that is growing in size (function v). The total 'growth' of the scene depends on both variables changing simultaneously.

section_3.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Gears
section_3.content: Visualize the chain rule as a system of gears. If Gear A turns Gear B, and Gear B turns Gear C, the speed of C is the product of the gear ratios. Formula: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).
section_3.example: A mechanical robot arm: the shoulder rotation (outer function) affects the wrist position (inner function). To find the velocity of the hand, you multiply the angular change of the shoulder by the reach change of the arm.

section_4.title: Interactive Synthesis: Putting it Together
section_4.content: Demonstrate a complex function that requires both rules. Explain the 'Out-to-In' strategy: peel the layers like an onion (Chain Rule) and look for internal products (Product Rule).
section_4.example: A rocket launch: the fuel consumption (inner) is multiplied by the altitude gain (outer). We calculate the total 'jerk' (acceleration change) using the product rule while applying the chain rule to the time-dependent fuel pressure.

section_5.title: Conclusion & Summary
section_5.content: Recap: Product Rule = 'uv' + 'vu' (derivative alternation). Chain Rule = 'Outside derivative' * 'Inside derivative'. Quick visual summary of the gear-and-rectangle animation.
section_5.example: A final visual cheat-sheet showing the two formulas appearing on a screen like HUD data for the robot from Section 3.
